entries.intent: Prove the host firewall is running before claiming the boundary control is in place

7.notes: The RHEL 7 STIG check reads the full unit status rather than a one-word answer; is-active exists on RHEL 7 but the pinned V3R15 check text is the status form, so this entry follows the check text it cites.

8.notes: The RHEL 8 STIG check narrows to the one-word service state. Reads only; it does not start, enable, or reload anything.

entries.verify: The command prints "active" (RHEL 8/9/10) or a unit block whose Active: line reads "active (running)" (RHEL 7).
entries.undo: Nothing to undo — this command only reads service state and changes nothing on the host.

stig.fix_cmd: yum install firewalld && systemctl start firewalld

entries.intent: Show whether an operator at the console can reboot the box with Ctrl-Alt-Delete

7.notes: RHEL 7 wants the target both masked and inactive; the pinned V3R15 check treats an active target as a finding on its own.

8.notes: The RHEL 8 check reads the same unit status and looks for "Loaded: masked".

9.notes: Same read on RHEL 9. The pinned V2R9 fix uses disable --now and mask --now, which the RHEL 8 fix text does not.

10.notes: Same read on RHEL 10 under the pinned V1R2 benchmark.

entries.verify: The unit block reports Loaded: masked and Active: inactive (dead).
entries.undo: Nothing to undo — this command only reads unit state and changes nothing on the host.

stig.fix_cmd: systemctl disable ctrl-alt-del.target && systemctl mask ctrl-alt-del.target
sudo systemctl disable ctrl-alt-del.target && sudo systemctl mask ctrl-alt-del.target
sudo systemctl disable --now ctrl-alt-del.target && sudo systemctl mask --now ctrl-alt-del.target
sudo systemctl disable --now ctrl-alt-del.target && sudo systemctl mask --now ctrl-alt-del.target

entries.intent: Prove the systemd journal is running before trusting anything journalctl prints

7.notes: No rule in the pinned RHEL 7 V3R15 benchmark maps to the journal service, so this row carries no STIG mapping and no RHEL 7 capture. The query itself is the same systemd read.

8.notes: No rule in the pinned RHEL 8 V2R8 benchmark maps to the journal service; the mapping starts at RHEL 9. The query itself is the same systemd read.

9.notes: RHEL 9 is the first pinned benchmark that requires the journal service to be active, as RHEL-09-211040.

entries.verify: The command prints "active".

entries.intent: Create a new logical volume of a given size inside an existing volume group
entries.verify: lvs <vg>/<name> shows the new logical volume at the requested size.
entries.undo: lvremove -f /dev/<vg>/<name> removes the logical volume — blast: red, see the dangerous-pattern table (dp-lvremove); back up first.

entries.intent: Grow an existing logical volume, optionally resizing its filesystem in the same step
entries.verify: lvs <lvpath> (or df -h on the mountpoint, if -r resized the filesystem) shows the new size.
entries.undo: lvextend only grows a volume; lvreduce is the shrink path and is destructive on most filesystems (unmount and back up first). There is no safe undo for a grow.

entries.intent: Create a new local account with a home directory, comment, supplementary groups and shell
entries.verify: getent passwd <username> shows the new account with a home directory and the requested shell.
entries.undo: userdel -r <username> removes the account and its home directory — blast: red, see the dangerous-pattern table (dp-userdel).

entries.intent: Add an existing account to one or more supplementary groups without removing it from any group it is already in
entries.verify: id <username> lists the new group under supplementary groups.
entries.undo: Read the account's CURRENT group list with id <username> before running this, then run usermod -G <that exact list minus the added group> <username> to restore it — usermod -G always REPLACES the supplementary group list, so omitting -a would drop every other group.

entries.notes: RHEL 7 uses chronyd by default for NTP (chrony package). The legacy ntpd daemon is available as an alternative from the separate ntp package but is not installed or enabled by default on any pinned release (RHEL 7 System Administrator's Guide, ch. 18-19) — chronyd is the only NTP daemon this toolkit generates commands for.
